subject: Deployment pathway economics — Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (post-call numbers + asks)
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@atlas-robotics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment pathway economics — notes & next asks

Samir — thanks again for the time today. Quick write-up from our side with the concrete follow-ups so we all have a single source of truth. TL;DR: you’re leaning toward Dedicated for latency/predictability but worried about commit size; Hosted looks simpler but needs confirmation on monthly token pressure. Private VPC is being evaluated for data residency and auditability.

Call highlights (rough):
- Workload: customer-facing agent + telemetry enrichment.
- Volume: you estimated ~2.0M requests/month (user-triggered), average ~560 tokens per request (input + completion).
- Peak concurrency observed in demo: ~85 concurrent calls, steady concurrency ~22.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for text generation.
- Data requirements: logs/trace retention for 90 days, encryption-in-transit + at-rest, possibility of EU-only in year 2 (but US-first).
- Main asks from Atlas: 1) simple break-even math (when Dedicated beats Hosted), 2) recommended reserved commit to cover steady traffic + burst, 3) Private/VPC onboarding plan & lead times.

Action items for Samir/Procurement:
1) Confirm the average tokens-per-request (you gave ~560; if we can get a 1-week export sample that’s ideal).
2) Confirm peak concurrency window (minutes of sustained peak vs spikes).
3) Any contractual constraints for commit (quarterly vs annual)?

What we’ll do (Redwood):
- Draft a short cost model (Hosted per-token vs Dedicated reserved commit math) and an easy table showing the break-even token/month threshold.
- Include a Private/VPC estimate (one-time onboarding + infra delta) and ramp plan.
- Send a workbook with assumptions so you can tweak numbers.

I’ve looped in Marissa (pricing lead) and Ben (solutions) to get the recommended pilot commit and a short technical note on meeting the p95 latency target. Expect the workbook and a 3-slide recap by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks —
Dylan
Dylan Brooks

- Requests/month: ~2.05M (that’s the active calls; we don’t expect heavy growth in Q4).
- Avg tokens/request: 560 (we’ll send a 7-day sample export by EOD).
- Typical steady concurrency: 20–28. Peak sustained (5–10min): ~80–95.

Procurement notes: we prefer to see both monthly consumption pricing (Hosted) and 12-month reserved commit options. For Dedicated we need a clear break-even and a recommended committed vGPU/hours estimate + expected overage rates. Also please include any SLA credits tied to latency uptime.

On Thu, Aug 20, 2026 at 9:12 AM Samir Patel <samir@atlas-robotics.com> wrote:

> - Requests/month: ~2.05M
> - Avg tokens/request: 560

Samir — appreciate the confirmation. Attaching a workbook (atlas_math_breakdown.xlsx) with the exact math; pasted below are the highlights so you have them without opening the sheet. The attached Redwood pricing playbook (excerpt) explains assumptions (model family, quantization, and batch gains we used).

Assumptions (conservative):
- Avg tokens/month = 2.05M * 560 = 1,148,000,000 tokens (~1.15B)
- Target p95: 350ms => we assume Dedicated configuration needs to cover peak throughput with headroom (90 concurrent).
- Hosted list (example): $0.00045 per generation token (includes model selection and streaming).
- Dedicated: baseline reserved capacity pricing: $42,000 / month for a 12-month commit sized to handle 90 concurrent with our recommended batching profile. Includes 24/7 capacity, autoscaling buffer, standard support. Overage rate: $0.00028 per token equivalent (if capacity bursts above commit).
- Private/VPC: one-time onboarding $32,500 (networking, certs, KMS integration) + monthly platform fee $9,500 + infra pass-through (we modeled infra ~10% above Dedicated for isolated tenancy).

Break-even math (approx):
- Hosted cost at current run rate = 1.15B tokens * $0.00045 = $517,800 / month.
- Dedicated committed cost = $42,000 / month (plus expected infra/ops) => immediate savings if usage is steady at the stated level (Hosted would be ~12x more expensive at this token rate).
- Break-even token/month where Dedicated becomes cheaper (using these assumptions) is roughly 90M tokens/month.

Recommendation for pilot (12–13 week):
- Start with a 3-month reserved commit sized at ~$42k/month equivalent (12-month contract priced pro-rata for pilot with conversion credits) to validate latency and RU provisioning; include an overage protection band (X% overage @ discounted rate) for the first 60 days.
- Parallel: enable a Private/VPC procurement track (we can start paperwork now) if you expect EU-only constraints in year 2. That path has ~6–8 week lead time once PO is signed (networking windows can extend).

Attachments: atlas_math_breakdown.xlsx (detailed token math, sensitivity table) and redwood_pricing_playbook.pdf (pricing assumptions & SLA excerpts).

Next steps:
- Samir: confirm you received the sample export (or send it).
- Procurement: confirm whether a 12-month priced pilot (monthly pro-rata) is acceptable or if you need a shorter P.O. structure.
- We can set a 30-minute follow-up next week to walk through the workbook and the pilot contract language.

If helpful, Ben can join to map the throughput -> qps -> GPU sizing.

Best —
Marissa Cole
Pricing Lead, Redwood Inference
